rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=4, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1500, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-5 ONE-KNOB: shared Adam lr 3e-4->1e-4 (per-scan-fit + warm-start both read cfg['lr'], solver_dual_ddomain_n2i lines 122 & 239). All other knobs held at the iter-4 WINNING baseline (n_iter=400, unet_c=16, pretrain_epochs=3, warm_start=True, val_n=4, grad_clip=1.0). FAILURE MODE / WHAT WE LEARNED: iters 1-3 proved the plateau is NOT optimization budget (n_iter 400->800: 0.9501->0.9508, marginal) and NOT capacity (unet_c 16->32: 0.9508->0.9502, NO gain). iter-4 broke the 0.9508 plateau to 0.9541 (+0.0033) by dropping lr 1e-3->3e-4 -- the per-image self-supervised fit has NO early-stop in the per-scan loop, so each single val scan can OVERFIT its own GT-free angular-subset measurements; lowering lr anchors each per-scan Adam fit near the GT-free warm-start init, trading raw fit for regularization. The REGULARIZATION/anchor lever is the only one that moves this solver. HYPOTHESIS (anchor-still-has-room): the demo_dl N2I sibling's BEST per-scan lr is 1e-4, one notch below iter-4's 3e-4; if the +0.0033 gain at 3e-4 came from anchoring nearer the warm-start init, pushing lr further to 1e-4 anchors even tighter and should lift val above 0.9541 (or, if 3e-4 was already the sweet spot, mildly under-fit and regress -- either way it localizes the optimum and tells iter-6 which side of 3e-4 to probe). EXACTLY ONE knob changes (lr); capacity stays at 16 (iter-3 ruled it out), budget stays at 400 (iters 1-2 ruled it out). Wall: identical step count to iter-4 (unet_c=16, n_iter=400, val_n=4) which ran ~13.5 min; outer_wall_s=1500 caps it <=15 min. grad_clip=1.0 mandatory (2304-view FBP adjoint overflows otherwise). DO NOT revert to amortized; per-image N2I rewrite (commit 1f4c3394).
